candidates.title: EdTech integrations: LTI 1.3 context, roles and service boundaries
knowledge_scope: LTI distinguishes a learning platform/LMS from a remote learning tool and standardizes their integration boundary.
LTI 1.3 uses a modernized security model and carries institutional/course context plus user role information without making those concepts a UI workflow.
LTI Advantage services add bounded concepts for names/roles provisioning, assignment/grade services and deep linking that can inform product terminology, state ownership and integration expectations.
excluded_methodology: education website information architecture, admissions journeys or content strategy
authentication implementation or security engineering procedure
generic product discovery, UX flow or QA methodology
candidates.expected_retrieval_value: Adds protocol-level vocabulary and data/service boundaries for EdTech integration tasks that the existing education website playbook does not own.

candidates.title: EV charging: OCPP 2.1 transaction and charging-system semantics
knowledge_scope: OCPP is the charging-station/backend protocol context, so product states should not silently collapse protocol/system concepts into generic loading or payment states.
OCPP 2.1 Edition 2 is the current 2.1 package on the Open Charge Alliance download surface and includes accumulated errata plus certification/test material.

OCPP 2.1 adds capabilities around ISO 15118-20, bidirectional charging/V2X, distributed energy resources and smart-charging behavior that may affect which charging/session concepts need explicit product truth.
excluded_methodology: generic state inventory, progress UI or error-recovery workflow
electrical engineering, charger installation or interoperability certification procedure
candidates.expected_retrieval_value: Adds EV-charging protocol semantics and current-version context so mobility product work can distinguish real charging-system concepts from generic UX states without turning OCPP into a UI recipe.

candidates.title: Generative AI products: NIST AI 600-1 risk-context vocabulary
knowledge_scope: NIST AI 600-1 is a cross-sector companion profile for generative-AI risks and risk-management actions, not a product-design workflow or compliance certificate.
The profile can supply reusable risk/context vocabulary for AI product framing while project-specific legal, safety and policy truth remains external evidence.
NIST states that AI RMF 1.0 is being revised in 2026, so any future canonical record based on this profile requires a freshness check before drafting or use in a time-sensitive claim.
excluded_methodology: human-AI interaction workflow for mental models, correction, confidence, override or graceful failure
generic trust/transparency UI methodology or regulatory compliance advice
candidates.expected_retrieval_value: Could add authoritative GenAI risk vocabulary that complements, rather than replaces, human-AI interaction methodology, but the active AI RMF revision makes immediate canonicalization premature.
